html:
The Tripartite Convention of 1899 divided the Samoan islands between Germany and the United States. Britain gave up its claims in return for rights elsewhere in the Pacific and in Africa.

Through the 1880s the three powers had backed rival Samoan chiefs in civil wars, and their warships faced off at Apia until the 1889 cyclone wrecked them. The convention ended the shared rule.

The western islands became German Samoa, later independent Samoa. The eastern islands, Tutuila and Manuʻa, went to the United States through the cession of Tutuila and became American Samoa. One people now live under two flags.
sum: The Tripartite Convention of 1899 divided the Samoan islands between Germany and the United States. Britain gave up its claims in return for rights elsewhere in the Pacific and in Africa.
